tools.name: submit_urls
tools.description: Submits a list of URLs to be checked and returns a job_id. Lists of up to about 200 URLs complete inline, waiting up to 60 seconds, and the results are returned directly. Larger lists return immediately with the job_id alone, and their results become available as the job progresses.

tools.name: get_job_status
tools.description: Get the current status and progress of a job.

tools.name: get_job_results
tools.description: Fetch paginated results for a job. Each result has the URL, HTTP status code (null if unreachable), response time in ms, and an error message if the check failed.

tools.name: get_verified_domains
tools.description: Lists the domains this account has proven ownership of. Checks against a verified domain run substantially faster than checks against an unverified one. Verification is interactive, requiring a DNS TXT record or a meta tag, and is done in the web dashboard rather than through this API.

tools.name: get_usage
tools.description: Returns the number of URL checks currently available on this account.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: submit_urls, get_job_results, get_usage · Private data: get_verified_domains · Public sink: submit_urls · Destructive: get_verified_domains.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: submit_urls, get_job_results, get_usage · Private data: get_verified_domains · Public sink: submit_urls · Destructive: get_verified_domains

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
